status_summary: The US special envoy for Syria said on 2026-01-20 that the Syrian Democratic Forces' role as the main ground partner against the Islamic State had largely ended after the Syrian government joined the coalition, and that the US has no interest in a long-term military presence; an agreement of 2026-01-29, described by Al Jazeera as US-brokered, provides for integrating the SDF into the Syrian army. US Central Command reported that US forces completed their departure from the al-Tanf Garrison on 2026-02-11 as part of a conditions-based transition, and the EU Agency for Asylum reports a US announcement on 2026-04-16 that the withdrawal from Syria was complete. At the NATO summit in Ankara on 2026-07-07 the President said sanctions on Turkiye would be lifted and that he would consider selling F-35 jets; a law-firm sanctions update of 2026-07-13 reported no formal sanctions removal or F-35 certification, and none was found later.

timeline.event: The US special envoy for Syria said on X that the SDF's role as the main anti-Islamic State ground force had ended, that an integration agreement would fold fighters into the Syrian army as individuals, and that the US has no interest in a long-term military presence.

An agreement described by Al Jazeera as US-brokered was reached on integrating the SDF into the Syrian army, after an earlier integration agreement of 2026-01-18 reported by Enab Baladi and Syrian government advances in the northeast.

US forces of the coalition task force completed their departure from the al-Tanf Garrison in Syria, which US Central Command described as part of a deliberate, conditions-based transition; the release does not mention the SDF or Turkiye.

The United States announced that it had completed its withdrawal from Syria and handed over its last base, Qasrak air base in Hasaka (as reported by the EU Agency for Asylum, which did not independently verify the announcement).
